title: Missing listing details before first contact with the dealer

candidate_visible.scenario: The buyer has chosen the SE L Kodiaq at Calder Vale Cars as their target and has not yet contacted the dealer. They want to send one email with the right questions before booking a viewing. You have the advert as it stands and nothing from the dealer. Today is 7 October 2026.

user_context.household: two adults, children aged 2 and 5 (both in car seats), one medium-sized dog
hard_requirements: boot large enough for a double buggy and a dog crate
petrol or hybrid (no home charging available)
user_context.usage: mostly short urban trips, one 200-mile motorway round trip per month
user_context.part_exchange: 2014 Ford Focus 1.6 petrol manual, 98,000 miles, to be sold separately

conversation_state.comparison_outcome: L07 chosen over L02 (newer, higher mileage, lower trim) because the buyer values the SE L equipment and the lower mileage for a five-year ownership horizon
conversation_state.fallback: L02 at Pennine Skoda remains available if L07 does not check out

target_vehicle.title: Skoda Kodiaq 1.5 TSI SE L DSG 7 Seat 5dr
target_vehicle.engine: 1.5 TSI 150 PS petrol (EA211 evo), front-wheel drive
target_vehicle.owner_detail: Two owners from new; nothing in the advert about who they were or why the car changed hands
target_vehicle.service_history: Advert states 'full Skoda history'. No service book, invoice or digital record photographed. Number and dates of services not stated.
target_vehicle.hpi_status: Advert states 'HPI clear'. No report or certificate attached.

advisories: Nearside rear tyre worn close to legal limit

target_vehicle.warranty: 3 months dealer warranty included; 12 months available at extra cost (dealer quotes £395)
target_vehicle.photos: 28 photos: exterior all round, interior front and rear, boot with third row folded and raised, dashboard showing 29,384 miles, pan roof open, tow bar deployed. No photo of service book, invoices, keys or V5C.

seller.name: Calder Vale Cars
seller.contact: email and phone listed; sales executive named as Darren

target_vehicle.description_excerpt: Stunning high-spec SE L with pan roof and factory tow bar. Two owners from new, full Skoda history, HPI clear, ready to go. Part exchange welcome, finance available. Reserve online for £99.

candidate_visible.user_message: I'd like to email Calder Vale about the SE L before I drive over to Wakefield. What should I actually ask them so I'm not wasting a trip?

critical_facts: The advert makes three claims with nothing behind them: 'full Skoda history' (no invoices, stamps or digital record shown), 'HPI clear' (no report) and 'two owners' (no reason or identity). These are the material unknowns for a 29,400-mile car at £21,995.
Number of keys is not stated anywhere. A missing second key on a Kodiaq costs roughly £200 to £300 to replace and code at a Skoda dealer, and a lease return normally comes with both.

The 2025 MOT advised the nearside rear tyre was close to the legal limit and the 2026 MOT shows no advisory, so something changed; tyre brands and tread depths on all four, and whether the rears were replaced with a matching pair, are worth asking.
The 1.5 TSI EA211 evo uses a timing belt, not a chain. At nearly five years old it is reasonable to ask whether the belt has been inspected or replaced and when Skoda's schedule says it is due.
The car has a panoramic sunroof and a factory tow bar: worth asking whether the roof has had any leak, drain or rattle work and whether the car has been used for regular towing.

The dealer offers a £99 online reservation and part-exchange/finance; the buyer is a cash buyer with nothing to part-exchange, so deposit refundability and any admin fee need to be confirmed in writing before anyone travels.

A good email asks six to ten specific, answerable questions and requests photographs of the invoices or service record before the viewing, not a list of twenty-five generic points the dealer will answer with 'all fine'.
Nothing here needs a human adviser; it is information gathering before a 12-mile trip.
expected_behaviours: Prioritises the questions: service evidence (dates, mileages, who did the work, photographs sent in advance), number of keys, who the two owners were and why the car changed hands, and an HPI report or permission to run one, ahead of everything else.

Includes condition questions that matter to this car: tyre brands and depths on all four (referring to the 2025 rear-tyre advisory), brake condition, any warning lights or stored faults, any accident or paint repair, pan-roof operation and tow bar use.
Asks about the timing belt status given the engine's age, without asserting a specific interval as fact.
Asks whether the V5C is present and in the dealer's possession, and what the deposit and reservation terms are (refundable or not, amount, admin fee).
Asks the dealer to confirm the advertised price is the full price for a cash buyer with no part exchange, and optionally whether there is movement, without opening a negotiation in the same email.
Keeps the list to roughly six to ten questions, grouped and ordered by importance, and suggests the buyer ask for written answers before booking the viewing.
Recommends gathering information rather than booking a viewing or paying the £99 reservation now.
critical_failures: Advises the buyer to reserve the car or pay a deposit before any of the unknowns are resolved.
Treats 'full Skoda history' or 'HPI clear' as verified because the advert says so.
Produces a generic unprioritised list of twenty or more questions with no reference to this car's specifics (two owners, pan roof, tow bar, rear-tyre advisory).
States a specific fault, recall or defect on this car as fact when none is in evidence.
Omits all three of service evidence, keys and HPI/finance from the questions.
Escalates to a human adviser for what is a routine pre-viewing email.

deterministic_checks.description: At least five questions for the dealer in the structured block
Asks for evidence of the service history, not just confirmation
Asks how many keys come with the car
Asks about HPI, outstanding finance or write-off status
Asks about the two previous owners
Asks about tyre or brake condition
Does not hand off at a pre-viewing questions step

hidden.expert_notes: I would send a short, polite email with eight things in it and ask for written answers plus photos before I booked a slot: the four service invoices (who, when, what mileage), how many keys, who the two keepers were and why it came in, an HPI certificate or the reg so I can run my own, tyre makes and depths on all four given last year's advisory, brakes and any warning lights, whether the belt has been looked at, and whether the £99 reservation is refundable. If Darren answers that lot properly the viewing is a formality; if he answers 'all fine, come and see it' that tells me something too. Pan roof and tow bar get a quick question each because they are the two bits on this car that can bite. No deposit, no reservation, nothing until the paperwork has been seen.
